query: For a CoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy matrix evaluated in sliding from room temperature to 800 °C, what single intervention could overcome the difficulty of maintaining low coefficient of friction and wear rate throughout the full temperature range? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains the mechanism expected to operate across the test regime, predicts performance relative to the starting CoCrFeNi material, specifies relevant temperature, load, and environmental boundaries, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes a controlled falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Microalloying equiatomic CoCrFeNi with a small amount of boron (≈1–2 at.%) will enable the in-situ formation of a continuous, glassy borate (B2O3-rich) tribofilm under sliding in air that, together with modest boride-strengthening of the matrix, maintains a low coefficient of friction and low wear rate from room temperature up to 800 °C relative to undoped CoCrFeNi.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy, single-phase fcc, homogenized, polished (Ra < 20 nm), no deliberate second phases; baseline hardness typical of CoCrFeNi.
generation.intervention: Add 1–2 at.% B to the CoCrFeNi matrix via vacuum arc melting or powder metallurgy, followed by homogenization to retain predominantly fcc matrix with dispersed nanometric M2B/M3B2-type borides (avoiding a continuous boride network).
generation.conditions: Pin-on-disk sliding in laboratory air (∼40–60% RH) from 25 °C to 800 °C; alumina (Al2O3) counterface, 6 mm diameter ball; normal load 5 N; sliding speed 0.1 m/s; total sliding distance 1 km per temperature; 30 min thermal soak at target temperature before sliding.
generation.structural_mediator: A self-assembled B-enriched, B2O3/metal-borate glassy tribofilm (~50–200 nm) on the wear track, blended with native oxides (e.g., Cr2O3/Fe-oxides), plus fine boride precipitates in the near-surface matrix that raise hardness and limit junction growth.
generation.mechanism: During sliding in air, tribo-oxidation of B at nascent surfaces forms a borate (B2O3-rich) glass that: (i) at room temperature hydrates to low-shear borate layers in humid air; (ii) above its glass transition/softening (≈300–450 °C) flows and self-heals, maintaining coverage and low interfacial shear; concurrently, dispersed borides increase substrate hardness and reduce real contact area and junction strength, lowering both friction and material removal. The composite borate–oxide tribofilm acts as a sacrificial, lubricious third body across the full temperature range.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to undoped CoCrFeNi tested identically, the B-doped alloy will show consistently lower steady-state friction and wear from 25–800 °C. Expected direction and approximate size: friction reduced by ~20–40% at 25 °C and ~30–50% at 600–800 °C; specific wear rate reduced by ~2–5× at 25 °C and ~5–10× at 600–800 °C. Benefits should be most pronounced above ~400 °C where the borate film softens and flows.
generation.baseline: Undoped CoCrFeNi HEA, processed and tested under the same conditions (air, 25–800 °C, Al2O3 counterface, 5 N, 0.1 m/s, 1 km).
generation.boundary: Requires an oxidizing, mildly humid environment to form and sustain the borate film; benefits diminish in dry inert atmospheres. B content should remain within ~0.5–2 at.% to avoid a brittle, continuous boride network; loads producing Hertzian contact stresses ≲1 GPa and sliding speeds ≲0.2 m/s to prevent rapid film expulsion; counterpart roughness ≤20 nm Ra. Above ~800 °C, chemistry and volatility may change; below ~10% RH at room temperature, hydration-assisted lubricity is reduced.
generation.uncertainty: Quantitative magnitudes are uncertain without direct measurements on CoCrFeNi–B; stability of the borate film under higher speeds/loads or in dry/inert atmospheres is uncertain; excessive boride formation could embrittle the near-surface and negate benefits.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two alloys: (A) CoCrFeNi (baseline) and (B) CoCrFeNi–1.5 at.% B, both homogenized and polished. Conduct pin-on-disk tests in air at 25, 400, and 800 °C (Al2O3 ball, 5 N, 0.1 m/s, 1 km; 30 min pre-soak at temperature). Repeat 25 °C tests in dry Ar (<1% RH) to probe humidity dependence. Post-test, analyze wear tracks and counterfaces.
measurements: Coefficient of friction vs time at each temperature
Specific wear rate from 3D profilometry of wear track volume and counterface scar
Surface chemistry of wear tracks by XPS/ToF-SIMS (B, B–O species, metal borates, Cr2O3, Fe-oxides)
Cross-sectional TEM/EDS/EELS of wear track to measure tribofilm thickness and B/O distribution
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: Hypothesis is falsified if any of the following hold: (i) no B enrichment and no borate (B–O) species are detected in the wear track at any temperature; (ii) at both 25 °C and 800 °C, the B-doped alloy fails to achieve statistically lower mean steady-state friction and lower specific wear rate than the baseline (p < 0.05); or (iii) the proposed B range (≈1–2 at.%) produces brittle spallation leading to equal or higher wear than baseline in air.
